newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's parliament adopts election draft law.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's parliament adopts election draft law.

text.p: Morocco's parliament unanimously adopted a draft law on general elections which are expected to take place in the second half of 1997 in Morocco and the disputed Western Sahara, a spokesman said on Monday.
"The draft law on the future general elections was unanimously adopted by the 333-seat Chamber of Representatives during an extraordinary session on Monday evening," the spokesman told Reuters.
"Five other draft laws, including those related to the status of chambers of commerce and industry were also approved," he said.
A detailed official statement on the election law will be released on Tuesday, he said.

The Interior Ministry said earlier that the new election law is part of the constitutional reforms adopted in 1996, including the establishment of a bi-cameral parliament to be elected in the second half of 1997.

Last week parliament adopted a law on the regions, aimed at reinforcing the administrative decentralisation policy and transferring some financial powers from the state to local authorities, including tax collection and funding for school and hospital building, it noted.
